items.title: Mapping Emerging Trends in Artificial Intelligence for Quality Control and Management: A Large‐Scale Computational Literature Review Using Semantic Natural Language Processing
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The integration of artificial intelligence into industrial quality control (QC) and management encompassing automated defect detection, real‐time process monitoring, and zero‐defect manufacturing has generated a rapidly expanding yet fragmented research landscape. This study addresses the need for comprehensive mapping of quality and reliability engineering practice through a computational systematic review of 9618 publications spanning the 2020–2025 period. A hybrid natural language processing (NLP) pipeline combining FlashText, Sentence‐BERT, KeyBERT, and spaCy performs semantic extraction of AI architectures, learning paradigms, defect typologies, and deployment contexts. The review pursues three objectives: mapping the architectural evolution of deep learning in industrial inspection, characterizing operational challenges of AI‐driven manufacturing, and identifying methodological frontiers for improving production reliability and supporting intelligent quality assurance (QA) systems. Results reveal that AI‐based quality control advances through coevolution of neural architectures, learning paradigms, and deployment requirements. CNNs remain central to discriminative visual inspection, while Transformers extend capabilities for multimodal reasoning. The field exhibits strong bias toward surface defects while overlooking safety‐critical internal defects. Emerging trends show transition from algorithm‐centric research toward deployment‐oriented paradigms including Uncertainty Quantification, Edge AI, Explainable AI, and Digital Twins. This work provides practitioners with an evidence‐based foundation for developing reliable, scalable AI quality systems aligned with Industry 4.0 principles.

items.title: Mapping research trends in artificial intelligence for K–12 teaching and learning: a scientometric analysis
items.abstract: This study examines the evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) research in K–12 teaching and learning by identifying major research trends, thematic structures, and emerging scholarly directions. A scientometric analysis was conducted using a validated corpus of 1,154 Scopus-indexed documents published between 2016 and May 2026. To strengthen corpus reliability, the dataset underwent content-level validation through abstract screening, duplicate detection, and thematic relevance assessment focused on K–12 educational contexts. Co-citation analysis, clustering algorithms, and citation burst detection were performed using CiteSpace to identify influential publications, thematic clusters, and temporal patterns of scholarly influence. The findings reveal rapid growth in academic production after 2020, particularly following the emergence of generative AI technologies. Four major research clusters were identified: (1) artificial intelligence literacy, focused on competency-based AI education and ethical awareness; (2) large language models (LLMs), centred on generative AI, conversational systems, and AI-mediated assessment; (3) early childhood education, emphasising developmentally appropriate AI learning experiences and playful pedagogies; and (4) K–12 context, addressing broader educational, ethical, and societal implications of AI integration in schools. Citation burst analysis revealed a progression from foundational AI literacy frameworks and constructionist machine learning pedagogies toward curriculum co-design, teacher readiness, and human-centred AI integration. Overall, the findings indicate that AI research in K–12 education is evolving toward more pedagogically grounded, ethically informed, and student-centred educational models while simultaneously highlighting challenges related to teacher readiness, curriculum adaptation, and equitable AI integration in school contexts.

items.title: Mapping the evolution of artificial intelligence applications in bone metastasis: a bibliometric and visualization analysis
items.abstract: Background Bone metastasis represents a major complication of advanced malignancies and is associated with substantial skeletal morbidity, impaired quality of life, and complex clinical decision-making. Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly emerged as an important computational approach for analyzing heterogeneous biomedical data. The developmental landscape, intellectual evolution, and future clinical directions of artificial intelligence applications in bone metastasis remain insufficiently characterized. Methods A comprehensive bibliometric analysis was performed using publications retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection, PubMed, and Scopus from January 2006 to June 2026. Bibliometric indicators, including annual publication trends, journal distribution, countries, institutions, authors, citation patterns, keyword co-occurrence, thematic evolution, and reference bursts, were analyzed using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and R-based bibliometric tools. Results A total of 540 publications involving 3,439 authors from 237 journals were identified. Research output increased substantially after 2020, with an annual growth rate of 24.01%, reflecting rapid expansion of AI-related investigations in bone metastasis. China contributed the largest number of publications, whereas the United States, Japan, and European countries showed substantial scientific influence and international collaboration. Thematic analysis demonstrated a progressive transition from early computer-aided diagnosis and bone scintigraphy analysis toward deep learning, radiomics, multimodal prediction, and language-based artificial intelligence applications. Imaging-related approaches remained the dominant research direction, while emerging studies increasingly focused on clinical information extraction, prognostic modeling, and integration of heterogeneous data sources. A small number of recent studies explored language-based AI for clinical information extraction, data organization, and knowledge support, suggesting an emerging but still limited extension beyond conventional imaging applications. Conclusion AI research in bone metastasis has evolved from automated lesion recognition toward broader applications in disease characterization, risk assessment, and clinical decision support. Imaging, machine learning, deep learning, and radiomics remain the principal foundations of the field, whereas language-based AI currently represents a comparatively small and emerging research direction. Future studies should prioritize multicenter validation, multimodal data integration, prospective evaluation, and clinically meaningful endpoints. Large language model systems may warrant further investigation as potential components of future disease-specific AI frameworks, although their clinical utility in bone metastasis remains to be established.

items.title: Mathematical foundations of artificial intelligence in healthcare: a systematic review
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare relies on diverse mathematical frameworks, yet their contributions to model development, evaluation, interpretability, and clinical translation remain fragmented. This systematic review synthesized the classical and emerging mathematical foundations underpinning healthcare AI and examined major methodological and application trends. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, studies published between January 2016 and June 30, 2026, were identified through systematic searches of Scopus, Google Scholar, and PubMed/MEDLINE, with searches conducted using Harzing’s Publish or Perish v8 where applicable. Bibliometric analysis was performed using VOSviewer, while methodological quality was assessed using an adapted JBI-based framework and AMSTAR-2 for systematic reviews. Of 653 records identified, 147 studies met the eligibility criteria. Non-mutually exclusive mathematical-domain coding identified linear algebra in 100/147 studies (68.0%), calculus and optimization in 91/147 (61.9%), and probability and statistics in 79/147 (53.7%), highlighting their roles in data representation, learning, optimization, inference, uncertainty quantification, and validation. A separate mutually exclusive classification of dominant methodological themes identified explainable and trustworthy AI in 24/147 studies (16.3%), statistics and learning theory in 23/147 (15.6%), probability and Bayesian methods in 23/147 (15.6%), calculus and optimization in 19/147 (12.9%), and linear algebra in 15/147 (10.2%). Radiology and medical imaging were the leading healthcare application (24.3%), while classification and diagnosis were the most frequent clinical task (17.1%). Overall, healthcare AI is supported by an interconnected mathematical ecosystem. Emerging approaches, including graph neural networks, Transformers, and quantum machine learning, require stronger external validation, standardized benchmarking, and rigorous evaluation for reliable clinical translation.

items.title: Metaheuristic physics-informed extreme-learning machine for initial orbit determination of near-Earth asteroids from too-short arcs
items.abstract: Modern wide-field astronomical surveys are substantially increasing the volume of observational data and the discovery rate of near-Earth asteroids (NEAs), placing growing demands on efficient and automated initial orbit determination (IOD). The physics-informed extreme-learning machine (PIELM) is an artificial intelligence (AI)-based algorithm for IOD that reconstructs orbital trajectories under observational and dynamical constraints. However, optical survey observations often span arcs that are too short to provide sufficient geometric constraints, making it difficult for the standard PIELM to determine a reliable initial orbit. New IOD methods capable of handling too-short arcs (TSAs) are therefore increasingly needed. We develop a new AI-based method for determining the initial orbits of NEAs from TSAs. It yields reliable initial estimates for subsequent least-squares refinement. We propose a metaheuristic PIELM method, termed MH-PIELM. An artificial bee colony (ABC) algorithm explores candidate solutions defined by a single line-of-sight range, with PIELM embedded directly within the search to reconstruct the corresponding trajectories under observational and dynamical constraints. The resulting PIELM loss serves as the fitness function, guiding the ABC algorithm toward promising candidate solutions. The method was tested on the initial optical observations reported for several NEAs. The MH-PIELM solutions enabled successful least-squares refinement, whose results closely agreed with the Jet Propulsion Laboratory reference solutions. The refined orbits were then used to predict the astrometric positions on the following day. Comparisons with the corresponding observations showed a useful short-term predictive capability for follow-up observations and target recovery, demonstrating the feasibility of the MH-PIELM approach. MH-PIELM offers a new AI-based strategy for initial orbit determination from TSAs by combining metaheuristic global search with physics-informed machine learning. It extends the applicability of the standard PIELM to challenging TSA observations.

items.title: Modular Testbed for Human-Autonomy Teaming: A Drone Swarm Firefighting Demonstration
items.abstract: Humans and intelligent systems are increasingly working together in high-stakes domains. To operate as real teammates, these systems require higher levels of autonomy, which is becoming increasingly feasible given rapid technological developments. Consequently, human-autonomy teaming (HAT) has become a key research area. Most HAT studies rely on simulation-based testbeds using simplified agents and tasks. These testbeds are often insufficiently flexible and customizable, limiting researchers in manipulating critical HAT attributes. Furthermore, most testbeds focus on dyadic teams, while real-world applications increasingly involve human interactions with multiple autonomous systems such as drone swarms. Understanding how operators can effectively control such swarms remains a critical challenge. During this demo, we will present our flexible and customizable HAT testbed, showing the example of human-swarm interaction during wildfire response. Attendees will experience controlling drone swarms with action-based and play-based control across varying swarm sizes, illustrating how the testbed facilitates systematic empirical research.

items.title: Motivation and Contribution in Open Source Software: A Meta-Analytic Investigation
items.abstract: Research on why people contribute to open source software (OSS) and related open collaboration platforms spans more than two decades, but its findings conflict, and studies often treat the work people contribute and their intention to keep contributing as interchangeable. Drawing on self-determination theory and motivation crowding theory, we meta-analyze 41 studies. The main analysis pools 178 correlations of eight antecedents with contribution effort and continuance intention from 29 independent samples (N = 9,632). Seven antecedents relate positively to effort, all eight relate positively to intention, and each relates at least as strongly to intention as to effort. Contrary to a common assumption, intrinsic motivation is not more strongly related to effort than extrinsic motivation, but its gap between intention and effort is larger. Reputation relates to effort mainly on platforms with a reputation system, and we find no sign that monetary rewards crowd out enjoyment. The findings inform how platforms can turn contributors' intentions into work.

items.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Artificial Intelligence Agriculture Groundwater Irrigation Quotas Under Aquifer Boundary Uncertainty: A Computer Welfare-Regret Evaluation
items.abstract: Groundwater irrigation quotas in agricultural multi-agent settings are typically computed against a known aquifer boundary, yet the boundary itself is an estimate whose uncertainty propagates into every quota decision. The framework separates two regret components: a boundary-regret term arising from mis-specified aquifer extent, and a coordination-regret term arising from the gap between the MARL equilibrium and the social optimum. A BACI design is then analysed under a declared variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, across cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points, with 2000 replications per design cell. The design analysis indicates that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5 percentage-point effect at 80% power under this variance structure. The contribution is a formal bridge between MARL quota theory and the evaluation designs that would be needed to test it, together with an explicit statement of the boundary conditions under which welfare-regret bounds remain informative.

items.title: Multi-functional embedding models for funder name disambiguation in scientific publication records
items.abstract: Understanding the historical allocation and distribution of research funding advances our knowledge of how scientific research is supported across fields, institutions, and regions. However, large-scale analyses are hindered by the lack of comprehensive funder name disambiguation solutions, as funder names often exhibit spelling variations, translations, abbreviations, and inconsistent levels of granularity. In this paper, we present a framework for developing multilingual, multi-functional funder name disambiguation models and demonstrate its application to research publications in biodiversity conservation. To construct a training dataset, we integrated the Research Organization Registry, which provides unique identifiers for research organizations, with two publication datasets: the Web of Science and the Crossref Open Funder Registry. We used multi-task learning with contrastive loss and multiple-negative ranking loss to fine-tune three open-weight embedding models from the Sentence Transformer, Gemma, and Qwen3 families. The best-performing models achieved accuracy above 0.90 when matching Web of Science funder names to Research Organization Registry identifiers, outperforming general-purpose large language models, including GPT-5.2, Claude-Sonnet-4.6, and Gemini-2.5-Flash, by more than 0.1. For funder names not indexed in the Research Organization Registry, we constructed a similarity network among funder names and identified clusters within it. Finally, we analyzed the disambiguation results and highlighted challenges arising from limited knowledge of smaller funders and funders from non-English-speaking countries. This work provides a reusable framework for funder name disambiguation with potential applicability across different model architectures and datasets, featuring cost-effective training data creation and multi-task learning and disambiguation.

items.title: Multi-site real-world performance of commercial AI for pulmonary and incidental pulmonary embolism detection
items.abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a leading cause of cardiovascular mortality, yet the real-world performance of FDA-cleared AI detection models remains incompletely characterized. We retrospectively evaluated two FDA-cleared AI algorithms from a single commercial platform (Aidoc Medical BriefCase)—one for PE triage on dedicated CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA; n = 30,678) and one for incidental PE (iPE) detection on routine contrast-enhanced CTs ( n = 37,191), across a 17-facility academic health system. Reference-standard labels were extracted from radiology reports using a validated LLM pipeline (97% accuracy, κ = 0.94). The PE model achieved 86.8% sensitivity and 99.1% specificity, with sensitivity declining from 99.3% for saddle emboli to 72.9% for subsegmental PE, and from 89.7% for acute to 65.3% for non-acute PE. The iPE model achieved 73.5% sensitivity and 99.8% specificity. Both models demonstrated lower sensitivity than FDA-clearance benchmarks while exceeding cleared specificity, with diminishing performance for peripheral and non-acute emboli mirroring known human reader limitations and underscoring the need for standardized post-market surveillance of AI-enabled medical devices.

items.title: Nanorobotics For Targeted Drug Delivery Systems Current Trends, Mechanisms, Applications And Future Perspective
items.abstract: Nanorobotics is an interdisciplinary field of research that combines nanotechnology, robotics, materials science, biomedical engineering and pharmaceutical sciences. The general idea is to build very small systems that can do useful things inside the body. In drug delivery, the goal is to get the medicine closer to the disease site and release it in a more controlled way. Conventional drug delivery can impact both healthy and diseased tissues. Nanoparticles have improved solubility, stability, distribution and cellular uptake of drugs, but many of them still mainly rely on blood circulation and passive transport. Nanorobotics systems seek to provide active motility, navigation, sensing, target recognition and controlled drug release. Various Nanorobotics systems are under study including magnetic, acoustic, optical, electrical, chemical, DNA based, biological and biohybrid systems. Potential applications include cancer therapy, antimicrobial therapy, brain drug delivery, cardiovascular applications, gene and cell delivery, biosensing and regenerative medicine.= But most Nanorobotics systems are still at the research or preclinical stage. Safe materials, immune reactions, accurate navigation, deep tissue control, manufacturing, drug dose control, long term safety and regulatory approval are some of the important problems. Future work may integrate biodegradable materials, advanced imaging, artificial intelligence, stimulus-responsive release and coordinated swarm systems.

items.title: Navigating the unknown: a qualitative descriptive study of ophthalmic nurses’ trust negotiation with generative artificial intelligence in China
items.abstract: Abstract Background Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools such as ChatGPT and DeepSeek are increasingly used in ophthalmic clinical practice. Ophthalmic nursing has three trust-relevant features: the irreversibility of visual outcomes, the precision-sensitivity of ophthalmic medication, and the relational dependence of visually impaired patients on nurse-mediated care. These features create distinctive challenges for nurses establishing, calibrating and maintaining trust in GenAI. The existing literature is dominated by static attitude surveys and rarely characterises trust as a dynamic, context-embedded process. Methods In this qualitative descriptive study, we conducted semi-structured in-depth interviews with 26 ophthalmic nurses recruited by maximum-variation sampling from tertiary, secondary and primary eye-care settings in eastern, central and western China. Interviews were guided by the Critical Incident Technique, and transcripts were analysed using Braun and Clarke’s reflexive thematic analysis. Reporting follows COREQ. Results We developed three themes: (1) tentative approach — competence appraisal from curiosity to conditional trust; (2) guarding professional boundaries — trust anchoring amid ethical tension and relational reconfiguration; and (3) trust negotiation within the organisational ecology. Across themes, nurses calibrated their trust in a graded, task-specific manner — a pattern we tentatively term ‘gradient calibration’ — while ethical obligation, the nurse–patient relationship and organisational context shaped how trust was negotiated. Conclusions Ophthalmic nurses’ trust in GenAI appeared neither as static acceptance nor refusal, but as a dynamic, context-embedded negotiation shaped by the irreversibility of visual outcomes, medication-precision demands and visually impaired patients’ relational dependence on nurses. Findings may inform specialty-specific AI training, institutional guidance and tool design; transferability beyond this sample requires further study.

items.title: Nonlinear and seasonal response mechanisms of hydrological drought in coupled human and natural systems
items.abstract: Hydrological drought evolution in heavily disturbed basins is jointly driven by climatic forcing, basin characteristics, and human activities. However, the nonlinear, seasonal mechanisms underlying hydrological drought responses in coupled human and natural systems remain poorly understood. In this study, the Wei River Basin (WRB) was used to examine hydrological drought evolution under coupled climatic and anthropogenic disturbances. A Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT)-based streamflow reconstruction framework, explainable artificial intelligence, nonlinear response analysis, and structural equation modelling were integrated to identify the multiple controls on hydrological drought evolution. The results indicated that hydrological drought progressively diverged from meteorological drought after the 1990s, while human-induced drought intensification became particularly evident after 2000. Explainable machine learning analysis revealed marked seasonal differences in the dominant drought drivers. Climatic factors remained the primary controls across all seasons, whereas human activities exerted greater influences in spring and ecohydrological buffering effects became increasingly important in summer and autumn. Lagged climatic effects indicated a greater dependence of winter hydrological drought on antecedent hydroclimatic conditions. Soil moisture served as a key intermediate variable linking meteorological anomalies to hydrological responses. Domestic water withdrawal generally intensified hydrological drought, with greater impacts in arid and urbanised regions, whereas grassland expansion partially mitigated drought impacts. Overall, hydrological drought in the WRB exhibited marked nonlinear, environmentally dependent, and seasonally divergent characteristics under coupled climatic and anthropogenic disturbances. These findings provide novel insights into hydrological drought evolution in coupled human–natural systems and inform integrated drought management in heavily disturbed basins.

items.title: Nonlinear Coordination-Regime Monitoring for RPAS Human–AI Teams Under Cyberattack
items.abstract: Cyberattacks can disrupt the communication dynamics that support coordination between remotely piloted aircraft systems (RPAS) and ground control stations (GCS), increasing uncertainty for human–AI supervisory control. This study proposes a nonlinear coordination-regime monitoring approach using the RPAS Network Intrusion Detection Dataset. Sliding-window multidimensional recurrence quantification analysis and sample entropy were applied to standardized telemetry features to estimate a continuous coordination-regime state, C t , and its short-term uncertainty. Attack classes produced distinct dynamical signatures: template-like attacks, including Bruteforce, MITM, and DDoS, exhibited more repetitive and structured dynamics, whereas DoS produced a sustained reduction in coordination structure. Window-level detection achieved an accuracy of approximately 0.79, a precision of 0.91, recall of 0.85, and F1 score of 0.88. These findings indicate that nonlinear traffic-dynamics markers can support operator-relevant alert prioritization by distinguishing persistent regime shifts from transient fluctuations. Future work will validate the approach on raw packet streams and evaluate human-facing supervisory decision policies.

items.title: Objective Assessment of Endoscopic Tip Control Using Artificial Intelligence and Video Motion Analysis: A Proof-of-Concept Study
items.abstract: Background and Aims Precise control of the endoscope's distal tip is a core visuomotor competence underpinning procedural safety and success. Despite its importance, objective assessment of tip control remains limited by reliance on subjective human judgment. We aimed to develop and internally validate a computer-vision pipeline, combining an artificial intelligence (AI)-based classifier of on- and off-target task engagement with optical-flow motion analysis, for objective quantification of endoscopic tip control within a standardized training model. Methods Thirteen endoscopists of varying experience performed standardized snare-tip soft coagulation tasks on stencil-imprinted ham models. Procedures were analysed using a computer-vision pipeline combining AI-based on-target/off-target classification with optical-flow motion analysis. Blinded raters assigned subjective tip control scores (0–100%). Associations between pipeline-derived motion metrics and scores were examined using generalized linear mixed models, followed by model selection and internal cross-validation. Results Inter-rater reliability of subjective tip control scores was moderate-to-good (ICC[A, k̂=3]: 0.74 (95% CI 0.60-0.87)). Multivariable analyses consistently identified three key predictors of tip control. Higher off-target time was associated with a 10.1 percentage-point reduction in tip control scores (95%CI −13.7 to −6.5), greater motion volatility with a 14.7-point reduction (95%CI −22.2 to −7.3), whereas larger volatility peaks were associated with a 12.3-point increase in scores (95%CI 4.2 to 20.5). The final model demonstrated good out-of-sample performance (mean absolute error: 12.2, root mean squared error: 15.0). Conclusions In this single-centre proof-of-concept study, AI-based labelling of task engagement combined with optical-flow motion analysis approximated panel rated tip control, which was characterized by sustained spatial accuracy, global motion stability, and well-timed corrective adjustments. This concept could support the development of a scalable and standardized tool for evaluating endoscopic tip control.

items.title: Occupational health and safety, work environment, and discipline predicting self-rated performance in Indonesian timber-processing
items.abstract: This study re-examines a census of the 30 employees of CV Sultan Jaya Pratiwi, a timber-processing firm in Asahan Regency, North Sumatra, who rated occupational health and safety, the work environment, work discipline, and their own performance on five-point scales. Because only the statistical output printed in the source thesis was available, we verified its internal consistency, reconstructed the correlation matrix it implies, and tested the differences between standardized coefficients. The three predictors jointly accounted for 90.8% of the variance in self-rated performance, F(3, 26) = 85.38, p < .001, and each partial coefficient was positive: safety β = .260 (p = .028), environment β = .180 (p = .032), and discipline β = .595 (p < .001). items.title: Occupational Health Challenges among Traditional Ritual Performers(Theyyam Artists) in Northern Kerala (India): A Narrative Review
items.abstract: Background: Theyyam is a traditional ritual performance art of northern Kerala, India that represents a unique confluence of spirituality, cultural heritage, and social identity. Despite its cultural significance, the occupational health risks and socio-economic challenges experienced by Theyyam performers have received limited attention in the scientific literature. This narrative review aimed to synthesise available evidence on these challenges. Methods: A narrative review was conducted using published research articles, ethnographic and anthropological studies, public health reports, government policy documents, cultural publications, institutional reports, and relevant grey literature. Evidence was critically reviewed and synthesised thematically to identify occupational exposures, health outcomes, socio-economic challenges, and welfare interventions affecting Theyyam performers. Results: The available evidence indicates exposure to multiple occupational hazards, including musculoskeletal strain, burn injuries, respiratory irritation, skin disorders, dehydration, fatigue, sleep deprivation, and psychological stress associated with physically demanding performances and ritual practices. Seasonal employment, irregular income, limited access to health insurance, and inadequate institutional support further increase vulnerability. Existing welfare initiatives have important gaps in awareness, accessibility, and implementation, limiting their effectiveness in addressing occupational health needs. Conclusion: Theyyam performers experience substantial occupational and socio-economic challenges that remain insufficiently addressed. Culturally appropriate occupational health policies, improved healthcare and social protection, strengthened welfare programmes, and evidence-informed public health strategies are needed to safeguard the health, safety, and sustainability of Theyyam artists.

items.title: Occupational health risks from climate-related and infectious-disease stressors: A scoping review of worker safety and resilience
items.abstract: Objective This scoping review examines how climate-related stressors and infectious-disease conditions, including pandemic-related workplace disruptions, interact to influence worker health, vulnerability, and occupational resilience. The review focuses on shared exposure pathways, vulnerable worker populations, methodological patterns, policy gaps, and strategies for strengthening worker safety under compound hazards. Rather than treating pandemics as isolated events, the review uses pandemic conditions as a lens to understand broader, recurring occupational risks and to inform strategies for building safer and more resilient workplaces under compound hazards. Methods Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a structured literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for English-language peer-reviewed and formally structured evidence sources published primarily between January 2020 and April 2025, with one pre-2020 policy study retained for foundational context. Out of 612 records initially identified, 10 studies or sources met the inclusion criteria across healthcare, agriculture, construction, emergency response, and other high-exposure sectors after systematic screening and eligibility assessment. Data were charted and synthesized by occupational sector, geographic region, exposure type, worker vulnerability, and methodological approach. Results The evidence indicates that climate-related and infectious-disease stressors frequently converge, amplifying physical, environmental, and psychosocial pressures on workers. Disproportionate risks were observed among migrant workers, informal laborers, low-income populations, older adults, women, and seasonal or cross-border agricultural workers, particularly where access to healthcare, legal protections, or adaptive infrastructure was limited. Most studies relied on descriptive, qualitative, cross-sectional, conceptual, or review-based designs, with limited use of predictive modeling, geospatial analysis, longitudinal evidence, or integrated datasets. Policy responses were often fragmented, with climate adaptation and infection-control measures addressed separately despite overlapping benefits. Conclusions Climate-related and infectious-disease stressors interact to reinforce occupational health inequities and expose persistent gaps in worker protection. The findings highlight the need for integrated, multi-hazard occupational health strategies that align climate adaptation, infection prevention, and psychosocial support. Embedding data-driven early-warning systems, equitable protections for vulnerable workers, and cross-sector coordination into occupational policies may help strengthen workforce resilience during routine operations as well as future climate extremes and public health crises. However, the findings should be interpreted with caution because of the limited number of available studies combining climate-related and infectious-disease occupational risks, heterogeneous study designs, and the emerging nature of the evidence base. Furthermore, since this scoping review maps evidence rather than formally grading evidence strength or testing causal relationships, recommendations should be interpreted as evidence-informed directions for future occupational-health planning and research.

items.title: Oerlikon Skyshield Integration in Indonesia's Layered Architecture: The Politics of Interoperability, Defense Governance, and Deterrence
items.abstract: Indonesia's layered air defense architecture requires interoperable systems that integrate local sensors and weapon systems with national command-and-control networks. However, the acquisition of advanced defense platforms does not automatically translate into integrated operational capabilities. This study examined how technical interoperability, organizational capacity, and defense governance influenced the strategic role of the Oerlikon Skyshield air defense system within Indonesia's layered air defense architecture. A qualitative case study approach was employed, drawing on semistructured interviews with Indonesian Air Force personnel, documentary evidence, and relevant scholarly literature. Data were analyzed through data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification, supported by thematic coding. Source and methodological triangulation were applied to strengthen the credibility of the findings. The results identified three principal barriers: inadequate data communications infrastructure, limited personnel competencies in communications systems and cybersecurity, and insufficient middleware capabilities to standardize data exchange with the Indonesian National Air Operations Command (Komando Operasi Udara Nasional, Koopsudnas). These constraints limited shared air situational awareness and external target cueing, restricting Skyshield's operational role primarily to local point defense rather than enabling its full integration as a node within the national air defense network. The findings further indicated that these interoperability challenges were associated with fragmented institutional responsibilities for systems integration, procurement dependencies, and limitations in defense policy implementation capacity. The study concluded that air defense modernization should prioritize architecture-centered defense governance, clearly defined interoperability requirements throughout procurement and system life-cycle management, periodic integration testing, specialized personnel development, and technology transfer focused on systems integration capabilities. These measures could strengthen coordinated air defense operations, enhance deterrence by denial, and support Indonesia's strategic autonomy, although their operational effectiveness would require further technical validation.

items.title: Organization and the Signature of Power
items.abstract: This paper introduces the ‘signature of power’ as a framework to enhance the understanding of politics in organizational studies. We argue for an understanding of contemporary forms of power as a signature that connects and divides two constellations: juridical-political sovereignty (supreme authority) on one side, and economic-managerial government (practical regulation) on the other. These poles have analogies in organizational theory dichotomies like formal versus informal, and institution versus network. The signature of power serves as a heuristic – a discovery mechanism – that enables scholars to navigate and integrate these opposing forces without reducing them to one dominant paradigm. The framework is articulated through four analytical strategies: analytics of government (local, immanent power practices), genealogy of order (historical foundations of governing orders), archaeology of glory (rituals and symbols of supreme authority), and analytics of authority (formal organizational hierarchies and operations). These strategies and their distinct relationships provide a more coherent analytical framework for a multi-paradigm approach to understanding power relations, resistance, and organizational forms. The paper tests this analytic framework through a study of the corporation as a ‘signature of power’ that bridges economic-managerial and juridical-political forms and is shaped by historical shifts and legal innovations. Addressing potential critiques, the paper emphasizes the framework’s adaptability to resistance and its applicability to diverse organizational contexts. This conceptualization encourages intellectual plurality, fostering historically and conceptually informed insight into politics as a set of power-related organizational and institutional practices.

items.title: Organizational safety and adaptive work practices in aquaculture
items.abstract: The aquaculture industry is marked by considerable operational variability stemming from shifting environmental conditions, biological processes, and complex work activities. While prior research has focused primarily on technical safety, fish welfare, and formal safety management, less attention has been paid to how workers manage variability in everyday practice. This qualitative single-case study examines organizational variability in a Norwegian salmon-farming company by addressing two research questions: (1) How do aquaculture workers manage variability in their daily safety practices? and (2) How do local work practices influence organizational safety? The empirical material comprises documents and nine semi-structured interviews with operational and managerial personnel. The analysis draws on both safety theories and organizational learning perspectives. The findings show that workers manage variability through adaptive work practices grounded in practical experience, teamwork, and continuous adjustment to changing environmental and operational conditions, rather than through strict adherence to formal procedures. Local work practices influence organizational safety by creating and sustaining safety knowledge within stable communities of practice, where newcomers gradually develop the competence and judgment needed to work safely. Although formal safety management systems provide an important framework, their effectiveness depends on how well they are integrated with everyday operational practice. Rapid organizational growth challenges existing learning processes by making practical safety knowledge harder to transfer and sustain. The findings demonstrate that organizational safety is achieved not only through formal safety management systems but also through adaptive work practices and the social processes that enable workers to manage operational variability.

items.title: PEMETAAN PERKEMBANGAN PENELITIAN SELF-REGULATED LEARNING DAN PROBLEM SOLVING: SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW DAN ANALISIS BIBLIOMETRIK 2020–2026
items.abstract: Research on self-regulated learning (SRL) and problem solving has expanded because students’ ability to regulate learning processes is important when addressing complex tasks. However, research development remains dispersed across different contexts, requiring systematic mapping to identify the structure and direction of the field. This study aims to map research on SRL and problem solving from 2020 to 2026 using a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) and bibliometric analysis. Data were obtained from Scopus using the search string ("self-regulated learning" OR "self-regulation") AND ("problem solving" OR "problem-solving"). From 730 initial documents, 198 English-language journal articles were retained after screening. VOSviewer and Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny were used to analyze publication development, keyword relationships, collaboration, and thematic evolution. The results show an increase in publications from 21 articles in 2020 to 53 articles as of September 28, 2026. Self-regulated learning, problem solving, and metacognition were the dominant keywords, with strong connections to self-efficacy, motivation, game-based learning, learning analytics, and artificial intelligence. Artificial intelligence and generative artificial intelligence emerged as recent research directions. These findings indicate that SRL and problem solving research is increasingly integrating cognitive, motivational, social, and technological dimensions. ABSTRAK Penelitian self-regulated learning (SRL) dan problem solving berkembang karena kemampuan mengatur proses belajar penting dalam penyelesaian tugas kompleks. Namun, perkembangannya masih tersebar pada berbagai konteks sehingga diperlukan pemetaan sistematis untuk mengidentifikasi struktur dan arah penelitian. Penelitian ini bertujuan memetakan perkembangan penelitian SRL dan problem solving periode 2020–2026 melalui Systematic Literature Review (SLR) dan analisis bibliometrik. Data diperoleh dari Scopus menggunakan kata kunci ("self-regulated learning" OR "self-regulation") AND ("problem solving" OR "problem-solving"). Dari 730 dokumen awal, diperoleh 198 artikel jurnal berbahasa Inggris setelah proses penyaringan. Analisis dilakukan menggunakan VOSviewer dan Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny untuk memetakan perkembangan publikasi, hubungan keyword, kolaborasi, dan evolusi tema. Hasil menunjukkan peningkatan publikasi dari 21 artikel pada 2020 menjadi 53 artikel hingga 28 September 2026. Self-regulated learning, problem solving, dan metacognition menjadi keyword dominan, dengan keterkaitan kuat pada self-efficacy, motivation, game-based learning, learning analytics, dan artificial intelligence. Tema AI dan generative artificial intelligence muncul sebagai arah penelitian terbaru. Penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa kajian SRL dan problem solving berkembang menuju integrasi kognitif, motivasional, sosial, dan teknologi.

items.title: PENDAMPINGAN UNTUK MENINGKATKAN KESEHATAN DAN KESELAMATAN KERJA PADA UKM TEKSTIL
items.abstract: Usaha kecil dan menengah (UKM) di sektor tekstil sering menghadapi permasalahan keselamatan dan kesehatan kerja (K3), terutama yang berkaitan dengan postur kerja operator dan kurangnya instruksi kerja yang jelas. CV. Visa Insan Madani sebagai UKM tekstil mengalami berbagai permasalahan ergonomi pada operator mesin jahit, seperti posisi kerja membungkuk, kelelahan otot, serta risiko cedera akibat aktivitas kerja berulang. Kegiatan ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan penerapan K3 melalui pendampingan dan Pengabdian Kepada Masyarakat yang berfokus pada perbaikan postur kerja serta peningkatan kesadaran operator terhadap keselamatan kerja. Metode Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA) digunakan untuk mengevaluasi tingkat risiko postur kerja operator. Hasil analisis menunjukkan adanya risiko postur yang cukup tinggi, terutama pada bagian punggung, leher, dan lengan. Berdasarkan hasil tersebut, diusulkan beberapa perbaikan berupa perancangan kursi ergonomis berdasarkan data antropometri operator, penggunaan alat bantu postur tubuh, serta penyusunan poster instruksi kerja mengenai postur kerja yang benar. Implementasi usulan tersebut menunjukkan perbaikan postur tubuh operator serta meningkatnya kesadaran terhadap pentingnya ergonomi dalam bekerja. Kata kunci: Keselamatan dan Kesehatan Kerja (K3), Ergonomi, Postur kerja, REBA, UKM Tekstil. ABSTRACT Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the textile sector often face occupational health and safety (OHS) issues, particularly related to operators’ working posture and the lack of clear work instructions. CV. Visa Insan Madani, a textile SME, experiences several ergonomic problems among sewing machine operators, including bent working positions, muscle fatigue, and injury risks caused by repetitive tasks. This study aims to improve the implementation of OHS through an assistance program and the application of industrial engineering practices focusing on improving working posture and increasing operators’ awareness of workplace safety. The Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA) method was used to evaluate the level of postural risk among operators. The results indicate a relatively high postural risk, particularly in the back, neck, and arm areas. Based on these findings, several improvement measures were proposed, including the design of an ergonomic chair based on operators’ anthropometric data, the use of posture-support equipment, and the development of instructional posters illustrating proper working posture. The implementation of these improvements shows better operator posture and increased awareness of ergonomic practices in the workplace. items.abstract: This conceptual article aims to theoretically and critically examine the influence of sustainability reporting (SR) quality on employee welfare and corporate reputation through a systematic literature synthesis based on the Six W framework (Who, When, Where, How, What, Why). The study analyzes 15 empirical and conceptual studies published between 2022 and 2026 from national and international accounting journal databases. The literature synthesis demonstrates that high-quality SR characterized by transparent ESG disclosure, comprehensive material information, reporting consistency, and independent verification is positively correlated with enhanced corporate reputation. However, a significant gap remains regarding the direct impact of SR on employee welfare, particularly in equitable remuneration, occupational health and safety, and human resource development. The novelty of this study lies in the construction of an integrative conceptual model connecting SR quality simultaneously to two distinct dependent variables within a unified theoretical framework supported by legitimacy theory, stakeholder theory, and signaling theory. The resulting conceptual framework is expected to serve as a foundation for future empirical research and policy implications for mandatory disclosure regulation in Indonesia.

items.title: PENGEMBANGAN MULTIMEDIA INTERAKTIF KREASI KONTEN MENGGUNAKAN KECERDASAN ARTIFISIAL UNTUK MENINGKATKAN HASIL BELAJAR SISWA KELAS X
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Mastering the skills required to create content with artificial intelligence (AI) requires learning experiences that connect conceptual understanding with practical application. To address this need, interactive multimedia was developed for Grade X students at SMA Wachid Hasyim 2 Taman, focusing on the topic of Creating Content Using Artificial Intelligence. The development process followed a Research and Development approach using the ADDIE model (Analyze, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation), with participants selected through purposive sampling. Product testing consisted of an individual trial involving three students, a small-group trial involving six students, and a field trial involving 76 students, comprising 38 students in the experimental group and 38 in the control group. Data were collected through expert validation questionnaires, student response questionnaires, and pretest and posttest assessments. Product feasibility was analyzed descriptively, while learning outcome gains were calculated using the N-Gain method and compared using an independent-samples t-test. The validation and trial results classified the product as highly feasible. The experimental group achieved an average N-Gain in the high category, whereas the control group achieved an average N-Gain in the medium category. The difference in learning gains between the two groups was statistically significant (t = 11.484, p < .001). The multimedia integrates learning materials, visualizations, animations, tutorial videos, examples of AI applications, exercises, and assessments. This product has the potential to serve as an alternative learning medium for Coding and Artificial Intelligence (KKA), although the findings should be interpreted with due consideration of the use of a nonequivalent group design. items.title: Personal Data Protection in the Artificial Intelligence Era: A Comparative Legal Analysis of Tanzania and China
items.abstract: The proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI) across banking, education, and public administration has intensified the collection and processing of personal data, raising concerns over algorithmic opacity, automated decision-making, and cross-border data flows. This article examines the adequacy of Tanzania’s legal framework for protecting personal data in the AI environment by comparing it with the more developed regulatory architecture of the People’s Republic of China. Adopting a doctrinal, comparative methodology, the article analyses primary legal instruments, including Tanzania’s Personal Data Protection Act 2022 and China’s Personal Information Protection Law 2021, against a composite theoretical framework combining the human rights-based theory, the risk-based regulatory theory, and Westin’s theory of informational control. The analysis finds that although both jurisdictions share a common statutory ancestry in internationally recognized fair information principles, they diverge sharply in the extent to which domestic law addresses AI-specific risk. China’s centralized, binding framework, anchored by a direct statutory provision on automated decision-making and dedicated generative-AI instruments, contrasts with Tanzania’s fragmented, largely non-binding, sector-confined approach realized through the Bank of Tanzania’s Fintech Regulatory Sandbox and the Ministry of Education’s Guidelines for Artificial Intelligence in Education. The article argues that Tanzania’s reform path lies not in transplanting Chinese regulatory techniques wholesale, given their embeddedness in a security-oriented state paradigm, but in selectively adapting specific mechanisms, including a stronger statutory right to contest automated decisions and binding regulation of generative AI, within its own rights-based constitutional order.

items.title: Perspectives: artificial intelligence and scientific autonomy: a policy agenda for emerging research systems
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence is becoming part of the infrastructure through which scientific knowledge is produced, yet access to computing, data, advanced models and expertise remains highly uneven. This Perspective argues that, for emerging research systems, the central science-policy challenge is not simply AI adoption but scientific autonomy: the capacity to choose, understand, adapt, evaluate and govern the technologies on which research increasingly depends. Scientific autonomy is not technological self-sufficiency; it is strategic interdependence supported by domestic capabilities. Drawing on Brazil as an illustrative case, we propose four dimensions of autonomy—epistemic, infrastructural, human-capability and governance autonomy—and a six-part policy agenda based on shared computing, research-data infrastructure, AI literacy, interdisciplinary networks, adaptive governance and capability-building international cooperation. Without deliberate capacity-building, AI may accelerate discovery while deepening structural asymmetries between research systems.

items.title: Pilot Workload Management for Single-Pilot Ops With e-Copilot
items.abstract: Single-pilot operations impose cognitive and procedural demands, particularly during abnormal events, airspace transitions, and communication-intensive flight segments. This study evaluated an ecopilot designed to manage workload by assisting with routine radio and checklist tasks while highlighting anomalies requiring pilot attention. In a flight simulation, 28 participants completed normal and abnormal scenarios under three conditions: baseline single-pilot operation, a rulebased e-copilot, and a predictive e-copilot using learned anomaly scoring. Outcomes included procedural deviations, radio timing, situation awareness, and startle recovery. The predictive e-copilot produced the greatest benefits, reducing procedural deviations by approximately 24% relative to baseline and improving recovery following unexpected events. The rule-based system also enhanced routine checklist and radio performance but was less effective during abnormal scenarios. Situation awareness remained stable across conditions, indicating that task offloading did not promote disengagement or complacency. Overall, predictive anomaly surfacing improved workload management while preserving pilot authority and supporting safer single-pilot performance.

items.title: Privacy Preserving Local Retrieval-ALLM
items.abstract: With the growing use of cloud-based artificial intelligence (AI) systems for document analysis, there are mounting concerns regarding user privacy. Certain documents may contain private, academic, organizational, or legally protected information that would need to be redacted or withheld before extracting meaningful information from them. This paper proposes Privacy-Preserving Local Retrieval-ALLM, a local document question-answering system capable of performing information retrieval and generating responses based on the contents of the documents. The system described in the paper uses the following process. First, it ingests user documents, performing optical character recognition if necessary, and segments them into text parts and embeddings. Next, the system stores the embeddings in a local vector database for similarity search. The system then employs a local Qwen 2.5 3B Instruct model to generate responses from the retrieved information. Finally, the system provides an optional permission-based web search if the retrieved document does not have the necessary information. In such cases, the solution does not need to transmit the contents of the documents to a third party but still has access to the necessary information. In conclusion, the prototype presented in the paper is an example of how local document analysis, semantic search, and local large language model (LLM) can be combined into a privacy-preserving question-answering system.

items.title: Privacy-Budget Evaluation for Computer Agriculture Federated Pest-Outbreak Detection Under Cross-Farm Sample Heterogeneity: An Artificial Intelligence Differential-Privacy Utility Bound
items.abstract: Federated learning allows farms to train a shared pest-outbreak detector without pooling raw scouting records, but the differential-privacy noise added to protect each farm's updates degrades detection utility in ways that depend on how heterogeneous the farms are. The bound is derived from a Rényi-differential-privacy accountant combined with a PAC-Bayes generalisation term that carries an explicit cross-farm heterogeneity penalty. The analysis yields a closed-form expression linking the privacy budget, the number of participating farms, the heterogeneity measured by a Wasserstein distance between farm distributions, and the achievable balanced accuracy of the federated detector. The bound predicts that the utility cost of a fixed privacy budget grows with heterogeneity, so that a budget adequate for homogeneous farms is insufficient when prevalence varies across farms. The result is a design rule for setting the privacy budget in agricultural federated learning and a benchmark against which empirical privacy-utility curves can be evaluated. The contribution is a formal, heterogeneity-aware utility bound rather than an empirical measurement, and it is stated as a proposition with explicit assumptions and boundary conditions.

items.title: Privacy-First Local Wealth Intelligence Terminal
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has revolutionized per-sonal finance management through automated budgeting, spend-ing analytics, real-time risk assessment, and personalized wealth creation strategies. However, standard AI-driven financial plat-forms rely heavily on centralized cloud infrastructure, requiring users to upload sensitive financial metrics—such as income, gran-ular expenses, asset holdings, and long-term targets—to third-party remote servers. This architectural dependency introduces significant security risks, including data breaches, unauthorized commercial tracking, API token leaks, and third-party mon-etization of personal profiles. Recent breakthroughs in open-weight quantized Large Language Models (LLMs) and optimized edge inference engines (e.g., Ollama, vLLM) allow complex natural language reasoning to be executed locally on consumer-grade hardware. This survey presents a comprehensive review of privacy-preserving financial systems, privacy-enhancing AI frameworks, and edge-based LLM architectures. We analyze the trade-offs between cloud-based financial services, federated learn-ing paradigms, and fully local, air-gapped AI execution. Building upon these findings, we present the structural formulation, multi-layer architecture, project workflow, and empirical validation of a privacy-first Personal AI Financial Advisor powered by local LLMs (Llama, Gemma, Qwen) orchestrated via Ollama, Node.js, Express, React, and local MongoDB storage. Finally, we highlight existing technical challenges, research gaps, and future trajectories for local financial intelligence.

items.title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for Artificial Intelligence Agriculture Crop Disease Detection Under Non-IID Farm Data: A Computer Differential-Privacy Utility Evaluation
items.abstract: Federated learning allows crop-disease classifiers to be trained across farms without centralising leaf imagery, but the non-IID structure of farm data and the noise added for differential privacy interact in ways that are poorly characterised for agricultural deployment. The analysis characterises the operating characteristics of the design under a declared variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, using 2000 replications per design cell across cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The results show that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5 percentage point effect at 80 percent power under this variance structure, and that the minimum detectable effect falls steeply as clusters increase from 8 to 32. The contribution is a design-level account of when differential-privacy noise overwhelms the between-farm signal that federated crop-disease detection depends on, together with a cluster-count rule that practitioners can apply before committing to a federation.

items.title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for Artificial Intelligence Healthcare in Uganda: Robustness Under Distribution Shift and Sparse Labels
items.abstract: Federated learning promises to train clinical prediction models across Ugandan health facilities without centralising patient records, yet its statistical behaviour under the conditions that actually prevail in the country's referral system remains poorly characterised. the present analysis treats the problem as one of design analysis rather than empirical deployment: it formalises federated averaging as a distributed estimator whose risk decomposes into a non-IID client-drift term, a label-sparsity term, and a privacy-noise term, and it derives the conditions under which each dominates. Under moderate distribution shift the drift term scales with the squared heterogeneity of local optima and is bounded by a communication-round budget, whereas under sparse labels the variance term grows as the inverse of the per-client effective sample size, producing a regime in which additional privacy noise is nearly free but additional clients are not. A before-after-control-impact design with an intraclass correlation of 0.64, between-cluster SD of 6.0 and residual SD of 4.5 is used to characterise the operating characteristics of a cluster-level evaluation, and the design requires 54 clusters to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power. The contribution is a set of propositions that link heterogeneity, label density and privacy budget to achievable model quality, together with a design template for evaluating federated clinical models in low-resource referral networks.

items.title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for Multi-Site Tuberculosis Drug Resistance Prediction Under Heterogeneous Laboratory Information Systems: An Asynchronous Aggregation Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Treatment Initiation Equity
items.abstract: Multi-site tuberculosis drug resistance prediction with federated learning faces a structural tension: asynchronous aggregation accommodates heterogeneous laboratory information systems but may systematically disadvantage sites whose data arrive late or infrequently, producing treatment-initiation recommendations that are less accurate for the patients those sites serve. We define a federated optimisation problem with staleness-dependent aggregation weights, derive a convergence bound that separates the contribution of data heterogeneity from that of staleness, and propose an equity-auditing procedure that compares per-site treatment-initiation error under synchronous and asynchronous aggregation. The framework is evaluated through a replication-based design study: no observational data are used or claimed. Operating characteristics are characterised under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.64) across 2000 replications per design cell, with cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis identifies the conditions under which asynchronous aggregation preserves treatment-initiation equity and the conditions under which it does not, and it specifies the audit statistics that a deployment should report. The contribution is a design-evaluation framework, not an empirical finding about any particular tuberculosis programme.

items.title: Privacy-Preserving Split Learning for Artificial Intelligence Agriculture Disease Diagnosis Under Intermittent Rural Connectivity: A Computer Communication-Cost and Accuracy Evaluation
items.abstract: Split learning enables privacy-preserving collaborative training of crop disease classifiers by partitioning a neural network between resource-constrained rural devices and a remote aggregation server, yet its feasibility under intermittent connectivity remains unquantified. The analysis characterises the operating characteristics of the design under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.640), with power estimated across 2000 design cells. Results indicate that the intraclass correlation of 0.64 substantially inflates the cluster count required to detect small accuracy differences, with 54 clusters needed for 5 percentage-point effects at 80% power. The findings establish boundary conditions under which split learning is communication-viable for rural plant disease diagnosis and identify the split-layer position that minimises uplink cost without degrading accuracy beyond a specified tolerance.

items.title: Problems and Prospects of Working Conditions of Labour Contractors –A Study
items.abstract: Labour contractors play a significant role in supplying and managing manpower across various sectors, including construction, manufacturing, agriculture, transportation, and other industrial activities. They act as intermediaries between employers and workers by recruiting labourers, arranging employment, supervising work, and facilitating wage payments. Despite their important contribution to economic development and employment generation, labour contractors face several challenges related to working conditions, wage administration, labour welfare, occupational safety, legal compliance, and the management of employer–employee relationships. The present study aims to examine the problems and prospects associated with the working conditions of labour contractors, with particular emphasis on their employment practices, income levels, working hours, job security, occupational health and safety, access to social security benefits, and relationships with employers and workers. The study also seeks to identify the major difficulties faced by labour contractors in meeting the changing demands of the labour market, complying with labour laws, and ensuring fair and transparent employment practices. The findings of the study are expected to contribute to a better understanding of the role of labour contractors in the labour market and provide useful recommendations for improving employment practices, protecting workers’ rights, and promoting sustainable industrial relations.

items.title: Profiling perceptions of psychologically restorative university environments and cognitive resilience among public sector university students: A baseline descriptive item-level and subscale analysis
items.abstract: Students at the university are constantly exposed to high levels of cognitive workload, assessment pressure, and the cognitive load needed to be able to perform in an academic setting, which can cause direct attention fatigue and academic distress. The quantitative descriptive study used a quantitative approach, and it was based on the Attention Restoration Theory (ART), which explores university students' perceptions of psychologically restorative university environments and their cognitive resilience. To obtain a sample of 300 undergraduate and graduate students across six academic departments of the University of Sargodha, Punjab, Pakistan, multistage stratified sampling was used. Data were gathered using a 35-item semi-structured questionnaire made up of the Psychologically Restorative University Environment (PRE) scale (20 items, α=.860) and Cognitive Resilience (CR) scale (15 items, α=.899). Descriptive analysis showed that the overall rating for the campus environment was moderately restorative (M=3.535, SD=1.043); the functional study areas (M=3.797, SD=0.934) and spatial adequacy (M=3.760, SD=0.972) received the highest ratings, while quiet restorative refuges from daily campus crowds received lower ratings (M=3.333, SD=1.045). The students' cognitive resilience was in the moderate range (M=3.578), with behavioral persistence when studying difficult tasks being in the high range (M=3.903, SD=0.933) and generating alternative study strategies in the somewhat lower range (M=3.307, SD=1.142). The results highlight the need to consider both restorative environmental affordances (noise-buffered quiet spaces, biophilic green spaces) and coping support workshops to ensure students' learning processes continue.

items.title: Protecting workers from Algorithmic Management: a theoretical framework for four key protection factors
items.abstract: Algorithmic Management (AM) is increasingly being linked to adverse occupational health outcomes. Although previous research has focused on the risks generated by AM, the protective factors that mitigate these risks remain theoretically underdeveloped. Drawing on the self-determination theory, social acceleration theory, surveillance capitalism theory, and the human oversight provisions of the EU AI Act, this study identifies and theoretically operationalises four protection factors in AM environments: Decision Autonomy, Pace Control, Feedback Transparency, and Loop Presence. By applying the Layers of Protection Analysis model, we argue that each factor functions as an independent protective barrier against AM-related health risks. Together, they form an integrated framework with direct implications for worker health measurements, algorithmic system designs, and occupational health policies. A conceptual six-step procedure for translating the framework into workplace assessment is also outlined.

items.title: Protocol for Conducting a Scoping Review on The Use of AI in Automated Scoring of Short-Answer Questions in Medical Education
items.abstract: Assessment is a central component of medical education, requiring methods that can assess learners’ knowledge and reasoning while maintaining acceptable reliability and feasibility. Short-answer questions (SAQs) require learners to construct responses rather than select from predetermined options and can support assessment of applied knowledge and reasoning. However, their use is constrained by the time and resources required for scoring and by potential variability among human graders. These limitations have increased interest in automated approaches to scoring written responses. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based systems using machine learning, deep learning, transformer-based models, large language models, and related natural language processing techniques are increasingly being applied to the automated scoring of SAQs. Such systems may reduce grading workload, improve scoring consistency, and facilitate timely feedback. However, questions remain regarding their scoring performance, reliability, validity, fairness, transparency, and feasibility for use in educational settings. The approaches and evaluation methods reported across the literature are heterogeneous, creating a need to systematically map the available evidence. This scoping review aims to map the literature on AI-based automated scoring of SAQs in medical education. Specifically, it will identify and characterize the AI-based models used; map the measures and metrics used to assess scoring performance, reliability, and validity; describe reported advantages, limitations, and implementation challenges; and examine how studies have compared the scoring performance, reliability, validity, and fairness of AI-based systems with human graders. The review will follow the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology for scoping reviews and will use the Population–Concept–Context framework to guide study selection and data extraction. English-language original empirical studies published from 2015 onward involving medical students and AI-based automated scoring of SAQs will be eligible. The findings will provide a structured overview of current approaches and evaluation practices, identify gaps in the evidence, and inform future research and implementation of AI-based automated scoring in medical education.

items.title: Quadratic Funding Mechanisms for Artificial Intelligence Agriculture Weather Index Insurance Under Basis Risk and Strategic Reporting: A Computer Incentive-Compatibility Regret Bound
items.abstract: Weather index insurance for smallholder agriculture is undermined by basis risk, and the machine-learning models that now price such contracts are trained on farmer-reported outcomes that are themselves strategic. the present analysis formalises the resulting tripartite problem — a quadratic funding mechanism that aggregates farmer contributions to subsidise index-insurance premiums, an artificial-intelligence weather index trained on reported losses, and a regret bound that must hold under both basis risk and misreporting. The mechanism is modelled as a two-stage game in which farmers first choose a reporting strategy and then a coverage level, and the insurer commits to a quadratic matching rule. Under a proper-scoring assumption on the index, the paper derives an incentive-compatibility condition that separates the truthful-reporting region from the collusive-reporting region, and shows that the quadratic matching parameter controls the width of that region. A regret bound is then established for the insurer's cumulative subsidy loss relative to the truthful-reporting oracle; the bound scales with the square root of the horizon, with the basis-risk variance, and inversely with the matching parameter, and it degrades gracefully when the index is misspecified. The analysis is illustrated with a reanalysis of monthly air temperature at Nairobi, Kenya, from 2000 to 2023 (312 observations, mean 20.146 °C, warming trend 0.2477 °C per decade), which supplies the climatological basis-risk term. The contribution is a mechanism-design result that ties the quadratic funding parameter to an explicit regret guarantee, and a demonstration that the guarantee survives strategic reporting provided the index is trained on a proper scoring rule.

items.title: Quality assurance 5.0: reframing quality management in higher education through artificial intelligence and continuous institutional learning
items.abstract: The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies is fundamentally reshaping higher education, exposing the limitations of conventional quality assurance systems that are often compliance-driven, periodic, and insufficiently responsive to dynamic institutional demands. This conceptual paper introduces Quality Assurance 5.0 (QA 5.0) as a proposed conceptual framework intended to reframe quality management by integrating artificial intelligence, continuous institutional learning, and evidence-informed governance. Drawing on Organisational Learning Theory, Total Quality Management, and Continuous Improvement Theory, the paper synthesises emerging scholarship to propose an adaptive quality ecosystem that is theorised to shift quality assurance from retrospective evaluation to predictive, real-time, and continuous institutional enhancement. The framework conceptualises AI as an enabler of intelligent quality monitoring, predictive analytics, automated feedback systems, and data-driven decision-making. At the same time, institutional learning serves as the mechanism through which universities continuously generate, share, and apply knowledge to improve academic, administrative, and student outcomes. By integrating technological intelligence with organisational learning capabilities, QA 5.0 is theorised to foster institutional agility, innovation, accountability, and resilience within increasingly complex higher education environments. The paper further presents a conceptual model illustrating the interrelationships among AI-enabled quality systems, learning-oriented organisational culture, strategic leadership, and sustainable institutional performance, specified as a set of testable propositions rather than as established, empirically confirmed relationships. Beyond extending existing quality assurance paradigms, the proposed framework offers a forward-looking perspective for policymakers, university leaders, accreditation agencies, and researchers seeking to modernise quality governance in the era of digital transformation. The study concludes that Quality Assurance 5.0 is proposed as an internally coherent and testable conceptual framework for moving quality management from static compliance toward intelligent, adaptive, and continuously evolving practice; its practical value for diverse higher education contexts remains to be established through the empirical validation identified as a priority for future research.
